description:
FILED s543q (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-28, CODE 6a1301ed = MAIN-READY-114 + records, v2-16500) by the Rosetta census B (docs/rosetta-plan.md section 6b; #2104).  Sized through one bounded heavy.sh leg (scratch/s543q/legs/heavy1.log, 00:09, load 0.7-1.0, the box otherwise idle), `/usr/bin/time` max RSS, the tree's `pcl` driver, each run capped at 90 s.

THE SIZE SERIES (the program's own loop bound N -> the last word's length; perl vs PCL):

    N (length)          perl wall / max RSS     PCL wall / max RSS        PCL
    31 (1.3 M chars)    0.25 s / 124 MB         0.90 s / 373 MB           same output
    33 (3.5 M)          0.69 s / 316 MB         2.54 s / 903 MB           same output
    35 (9.2 M)          1.83 s / 817 MB         2.63 s / 1,045 MB         Heap exhausted (no output: STDOUT buffered)
    37 (24 M, the program)  5.04 s / 2,130 MB   2.72 s / 1,045 MB         Heap exhausted

    WHICH CONSTRUCT (9.2 M characters, "ab" x 4_600_000):
    `my %c; $c{$_}++ for split //, $s;`      perl 0.90 s / 818 MB    PCL Heap exhausted at 1,004 MB
    `my @l = split //, $s;`                  perl 0.70 s / 818 MB    PCL 1.35 s / 935 MB (right)
    the word BUILDING alone (N = 37, no split) perl 0.03 s / 53 MB   PCL 0.40 s / 306 MB (right)

So the explosion is the per-ELEMENT cost of the split list in a foreach (about 3x perl's at 3.5 M elements, ~1.2x for an array
assignment), against a hard ceiling: tools/lib/PCLSbcl.pm passes no --dynamic-space-size, so every user program gets SBCL's
default 1 GB (a per-file allowance exists for the companion suite only, baselines/perl-suite-heap.tsv, #1590).  Even at perl's
own footprint the program needs 2.1 GB, so the ceiling alone kills it; the per-element cost decides where smaller programs die.
UNTIDY half: the death is SBCL's "Heap exhausted during garbage collection" + "fatal error encountered in SBCL" + a GC table on
stderr, exit 1 (perl: "Out of memory!" -- the same family as #2556's binding-stack form).

NOT TAKEN (outside the claim; for whoever sizes the fix): which part of an element is large (a p-box per substring? the foreach
alias list?) -- `(room)` after the `my @l` shape would say; and whether raising the default heap is acceptable on the gate's
8-SBCL box (#1590's argument against a global raise).

PROGRAMS: 0478-Fibonacci-word (class EXHAUSTED).
frequency_reason: Rosetta: 0478-Fibonacci-word (letter frequencies of a 24 M-character string: `$c{$_}++ for split //, $str`)
subject: MEMORY: a program whose data needs more than SBCL's fixed 1 GB dynamic space dies "Heap exhausted during garbage collection" + an SBCL fatal-error dump where perl grows to what the machine has -- and a foreach over `split //, $str` costs PCL about 1.2-3x perl's memory, so a 9.2 M-character split already dies (perl 0.8 GB) (Rosetta 0478)
triage_reason: exit criterion 4 (docs/supported-subset.md section 5: no open heap-exhaustion task inside the subset); split and hashes are core; memory itself is outside the correctness claim (section 2) -- sized here, not chased
